finding.summary: The evidence bundle checked summarized page counts and a single resource label but did not itself establish that retained response headers formed one complete, ordered, successful, resource-consistent sequence for each client.
finding.uncertainty: Runtime behavior remains unverified until the Node tests and authenticated traversals execute.

capabilities: Requires one ordered page record per client starting at page one with no skipped indexes.
Requires successful HTTP status and integer x-ratelimit-limit, remaining, used, reset, and non-empty resource headers for every page.
Rejects impossible rate-limit arithmetic, regressing reset epochs, within-client resource changes, and cross-client resource disagreement.
Produces the existing dual_client_retained_response_header_contract shape and fails promotion closed when either client observes zero remaining capacity.

source_status.primary: GitHub REST rate-limit documentation describes x-ratelimit-limit, x-ratelimit-remaining, x-ratelimit-used, x-ratelimit-reset, and x-ratelimit-resource as response-header evidence.
source_status.repository: Compared against the existing workflow evidence bundle and prior R-021 rate-limit page-count binding to avoid duplication.

design_implication: Construct the accepted summary proof only from validated retained per-page response records, then pass that proof into the existing evidence bundle. Do not accept a manually authored summary as equivalent evidence.
falsification_route: Run the committed Node test file in an authenticated checkout.
Capture every response page from both exhaustive clients and validate the records before bundle generation.

Reject this design if GitHub documents that relevant pagination responses legitimately change x-ratelimit-resource or regress reset epochs during one uninterrupted traversal; update the validator with a documented transition model rather than weakening it silently.
